title: Safe staffing and skill mix
blurb: Explain how staffing and skill mix affect safety, protect one-to-one care in labour, and act on NICE NG4 midwifery red flags.
question: On a busy labour ward, a midwife is asked to care for two women who are both in established labour. What should she do?

teach.body: SPM 5.5 asks midwives to understand the relationship between safe staffing levels, effective team working, appropriate skill mix, and the safety and quality of care. NICE NG4 says women and babies should get the midwifery care they need in every setting, at any time of day, any day of the week. Skill mix is the make-up of the team by qualification and experience. In plain English: not enough midwives, or the wrong mix, means care is missed or delayed.

NICE intrapartum guidance asks services to provide a model of care that supports one-to-one care in labour for all women. NG4 defines it as care provided throughout labour exclusively by a midwife solely dedicated to that woman's care, though not necessarily the same midwife for the whole labour. Established labour means regular, painful contractions with progressive cervical dilatation from 4 cm. Any occasion when one midwife cannot give continuous one-to-one care in established labour is a red flag.
teach.cite: NICE NG235 1.4.5; NG4 terms and Box 3

head: Red flag
Threshold
rows: Missed medicines; no full exam in labour; late action on abnormal vital signs
teach.caption: Plus delayed or cancelled time-critical activity. Trusts may agree extra local red flags.

steps.label: Notify
steps.sub: The midwife in charge of the shift

steps.label: Decide
steps.sub: Is staffing the cause? What action?

steps.label: Record
steps.sub: Even if no action was taken

teach.caption: NG4 does not rank the other options, but closure or cancellation is the last resort, and no action should cause red flags in another area of the service (NG4 1.1.11, 1.3.4).

teach.body: At 03:00, midwife Sian is caring for Laura, 6 cm and contracting regularly, when the coordinator asks her to also take Amira, 5 cm, because a colleague went home ill. Both are in established labour, so Sian cannot give either woman one-to-one care: a red flag. She tells the midwife in charge clearly. The midwife in charge calls the on-call midwife, moves a midwife from the antenatal ward, which has no women waiting, and records the red flag for review.

teach.h: Who counts in the midwife establishment
teach.caption: NG4 1.2.3. Establishments are set at least every 6 months and reviewed at board level at least every 6 months.

teach.note: Reviewed alongside women's survey results and outcome measures such as booking by 13 weeks.

teach.text: The midwife in charge decides whether staffing is the cause of a red flag. Your job is to notify her promptly; do not decide yourself that it 'was not really a staffing problem' and skip the report. Every red flag is recorded, even if no action was needed.

items: SPM 5.5: staffing, team working and skill mix directly affect safety and quality.
One-to-one care: one midwife solely dedicated to a woman throughout established labour (from 4 cm).
Red flags: triage delay 30 min or more, pain relief delay over 30 min, suturing delay 60 min or more, induction delay 2 h or more, no one-to-one care.
Notify the midwife in charge, who decides cause and action; record every red flag.
Escalation plans: closures are the last resort, and no fix should create red flags elsewhere.

summary: You can now explain how staffing and skill mix affect the safety of women and babies and protect one-to-one care in established labour. You can also recognise NICE NG4 red flags and respond to them in the right order.

A.q: According to NICE NG4, what does one-to-one care in labour mean?
options: The same midwife for the whole of labour
A midwife present for the second stage
A midwife caring for no more than two women
A midwife solely dedicated to that woman
A.why: NG4: care throughout labour exclusively by a midwife solely dedicated to her care, not necessarily the same midwife for the whole of labour.

whyNot.0: The midwife can change, for example at shift change; dedication is the point.
whyNot.1: One-to-one care covers all of established labour, not just the second stage.
whyNot.2: Caring for two women is not one-to-one care.

A.q: Which delay in giving pain relief is an NG4 midwifery red flag?
A.why: NG4 Box 3: a delay of more than 30 minutes in providing pain relief is a red flag.

whyNot.0: 15 minutes is shorter than the NG4 threshold.
whyNot.2: 60 minutes is the threshold for washing and suturing.
whyNot.3: 2 hours is the threshold for starting induction after admission.

A.q: A midwifery red flag event occurs on the postnatal ward. Who should be notified?
options: The midwife in charge of the shift
The head of midwifery the next morning
A.why: NG4 1.3.5: the midwife in charge of the service or shift is notified and decides whether staffing is the cause and what action is needed.

whyNot.1: Waiting until morning delays action; the shift lead acts now.
whyNot.2: Red flags are about midwifery staffing, managed by the midwife in charge.
whyNot.3: The red flag is recorded and reviewed later, but the immediate notification is to the midwife in charge.

B.q: A manager calculating the midwifery establishment includes three student midwives on placement. What is wrong with this?
options: Students should count as half a midwife
Students are counted for day shifts
Students count after their first year
B.why: NG4 1.2.3: base whole-time equivalents on registered midwives and do not include student midwives or supernumerary midwives.

whyNot.0: There is no partial counting of students in NG4.
whyNot.1: Students are excluded regardless of shift pattern under NG4.
whyNot.3: Year of training does not change their exclusion.

B.q: A maternity unit's staffing falls short of need on a night shift. Under NG4, which option comes last in the escalation plan?
B.why: NG4 1.1.11 and 1.3.4: consider service cancellations or closures as a last resort.

whyNot.1: On-call staff are an early option.
whyNot.2: Rescheduling non-urgent work is an early option.
whyNot.3: Redeployment is an option before closure.

B.q: A woman waited 35 minutes to be triaged, but she was well and the delay caused no harm. What should happen?
options: Note it informally, as no harm occurred
Record it as a red flag for review
B.why: NG4 1.3.5: record midwifery red flag events for review, even if no action was taken. A triage delay of 30 minutes or more is a red flag.

whyNot.0: Red flags are formally recorded whether or not harm occurred, to inform staffing reviews.
whyNot.1: An apology may be kind, but the red flag must also be recorded.
whyNot.2: This is a service issue, not a fitness to practise matter.

C.q: A midwife caring for a woman at 7 cm is asked to also take a woman at 5 cm with regular painful contractions. What should she do first?
options: Tell the midwife in charge it is a red flag
Take both women and ask a student to help
Refuse to take the second woman
Ask the obstetric registrar to cover one woman
C.why: Both women are in established labour, so she cannot give one-to-one care: an NG4 red flag. She notifies the midwife in charge, who decides the action.

whyNot.1: A student is not counted and does not replace a dedicated midwife.
whyNot.2: Refusing without escalating leaves the second woman without care.
whyNot.3: A doctor does not provide one-to-one midwifery care.

C.q: The coordinator plans to move the only postnatal midwife to the labour ward, leaving postnatal women without medicines for several hours. What does NG4 say about this?
options: Escalation must not cause red flags elsewhere
Support workers can cover postnatal care
It is acceptable for one shift
C.why: NG4 1.1.11 and 1.1.19: actions in escalation plans must not cause midwifery red flag events in other areas; missed medicines are a red flag.

whyNot.0: NG4 requires that one area's fix does not create red flags in another.
whyNot.2: Postnatal women still need midwifery care; delegation is within competence and supervision.
whyNot.3: Creating a red flag is not acceptable for any length of time under NG4.

C.q: A head of midwifery is reviewing the staffing establishment. Which is an NG4 staff-reported safe staffing indicator?
C.why: NG4 Box 4 staff-reported measures: missed breaks, midwife overtime, midwifery sickness and staff morale.

whyNot.0: Birth numbers inform demand, but are not a staff-reported indicator.
whyNot.1: The caesarean rate is not one of the NG4 indicators.
whyNot.3: Complaints may trigger review, but are not a staff-reported indicator.

reteach.title: Red flag, then the midwife in charge
reteach.question: What is the one thing a midwife must do when a staffing red flag happens?

blocks.body: A red flag is an immediate sign that something may be wrong with staffing. You tell the midwife in charge. She decides whether staffing is the cause and what to do, using the escalation plan: on-call staff, redeployment, rescheduling, with closure last. Every red flag is recorded, because the pattern informs the six-monthly staffing review.

blocks.text: Pain relief is 'more than 30 minutes'; triage is '30 minutes or more'. Both sit around half an hour.

explain.body: NG4 defines established labour as regular, painful contractions with progressive cervical dilatation from 4 cm. From then, one-to-one care applies.

test.q: According to NICE NG4, from what cervical dilatation, with regular painful contractions, is labour established?
test.why: NG4: established labour is regular painful contractions with progressive cervical dilatation from 4 cm.

whyNot.0: 2 cm is within the latent phase.
whyNot.1: 3 cm is within the latent phase.
whyNot.3: 6 cm is later than the definition.

explain.body: The midwifery staffing establishment is reviewed at board level at least every 6 months, including demand data, red flags and safe staffing indicators, and more often if quality falls or red flags increase.

test.q: How often should a trust board review its midwifery staffing establishment under NG4, as a minimum?
test.why: NG4 1.1.13: review the midwifery staffing establishment at board level at least every 6 months.

whyNot.0: Three-monthly is more often than the minimum.
whyNot.2: Annual review is less often than NG4 requires.
whyNot.3: Three years is the revalidation cycle, not staffing review.

explain.body: Skill mix is the composition of the midwifery team in terms of qualification and experience. NG4 allows for local skill mixes, including specialist and consultant midwives and practice development midwives, and for work safely delegated to maternity support workers.

test.q: What does skill mix mean in NICE NG4?
options: The number of midwives on each shift
The ratio of midwives to doctors
The range of tasks a midwife can do
test.why: NG4: skill mix is the composition of the midwifery team in terms of qualification and experience.

whyNot.0: Numbers are staffing levels, not skill mix.
whyNot.1: NG4's skill mix is about the midwifery team, not a midwife-to-doctor ratio.
whyNot.3: Individual scope is competence, not team skill mix.

explain.body: A delay of 2 hours or more between admission for induction and beginning the process is a red flag.

test.q: A woman admitted for induction of labour has waited on the ward. Which delay before the process begins is an NG4 red flag?
test.why: NG4 Box 3: a delay of 2 hours or more between admission for induction and beginning of the process is a red flag.

whyNot.1: 1 hour is the washing and suturing threshold.
whyNot.2: 4 hours is longer than the NG4 threshold.
